On 30 March 2025, members of the Gagauz and Moldovan diaspora protested in front of the Moldovan Embassy in Moscow - Central. During the demonstration people shared their support for the Governor of the Gagauzia Autonomy, who was arrested at the Chisinau International airport on 25 March, and their dissatisfaction with the current Moldovan government. Romanian sources found evidence of people being promised financial rewards for participating in the demonstration.

On 30 March 2025, around 100 shared equity holders protested and burst into the residential complex 'ZHK Ostafievo' in Ostafievo village within Novomoskovskiy municipality of Moscow. Residents who bought property in the turnkey development project demanded to be given access to their apartments, that they were promised to get in January 2025. People that got on the territory of the complex occupied their supposed apartments and refused to leave.

On 30 March 2025, local environmental activists protested on a government-sanctioned rally at a park in Yaroslavl. Protesters complained about several environmental issues, including local factories' emissions and deforestation.

On 30 March 2025, elderly residents protested and filmed a video addressed to the Speaker of the State Duma in Saratov. Locals demanded the dismissal of the MP, who, according to the protesters, insulted those residents who were advocating for the preservation of a local park.

On 30 March 2025, around 270 residents protested in Blagoveshchensk, Amur. Protesters, many of whom came with their pets, spoke out against the controversial parliamentary 'stray animals euthanasia' bill that is being discussed in the State Duma. Recently it was uncovered that not only stray animals, but also lost pets could be killed within the framework of the proposed legislation.

On 30 March 2025, a woman stabbed the Faculty of Philosophy dean in Nis. Upon stabbing her in the hand, the attacker shouted that the Dean 'ruined her granddaughter', alluding to the faculty blockades. The Dean was subsequently hospitalized. The government had repeatedly verbally targeted the dean for her support for students protests.

On 30 March 2025, health workers gathered in Jagodina, voicing their support for the blockading students' and teachers' demands for accountability for the loss of 16 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station.

On 30 March 2025, students from Pomoravlje gathered in Jagodina, demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and expressing solidarity with their colleagues in blockades. Together with local students and citizens they marched through the city and observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign.

On 30 March 2025, citizens, teachers and farmers engaged in a protest ride with their cars and tractors, and gathered in front of the Assembly building in Lapovo, voicing their support for the students' blockades and demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse. The protesters also observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign.

On 30 March 2025, students, teachers, and citizens gathered in front of the Gymnasium and Economy School in Leskovac, voicing their support to the students and teachers in the blockades, and celebrating 100 days of the blockade in Leskovac.

On 30 March 2025, students, teachers, and citizens marched through Nis, protesting against the government's political pressure on the academic community, physical violence directed at them, and financial repercussions through reduced wages. The protesters voiced their support for the students' demands and observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign.

On 30 March 2025, students and citizens gathered at the location where the Faculty of Philosophy Dean got stabbed earlier in Nis, protesting against the government inciting violence towards the academic community. The protesters denounced the frequent violent actions and expressed solidarity with the attacked Dean.

On 30 March 2025, students and citizens marched through Novi Sad, protesting against the physical violence directed towards the students and teachers in blockades, triggered by the recent event where the University professor got hit with fireworks.

On 30 March 2025, students gathered in Novi Sad, voicing their solidarity with the Faculty of Philosophy Dean who got stabbed in Nis earlier. The students urged the government to stop inciting violence.

On 30 March 2025, students and citizens gathered in Obrenovac, denouncing the attack and stabbing of the Faculty of Philosophy Dean in Nis. The protesters voiced that the government led by SNS is inciting violence towards the academic community, especially those in blockades.

On 30 March 2025, actors and theatre workers gathered in Sabac, protesting against the imposed systematization of work that led to numerous dismissals and 'technological redundancy' within their institution. The protesters also called for the dismissal of the incumbent theatre director.

On 30 March 2025, students gathered in Subotica, protesting against government repression, police brutality and targeted violence towards students in blockades. The protesters rate the government's actions as illegal and called for an urgent halt.

On 30 March 2025, students and citizens from several Serbian cities marched and blocked roads in Uzice, demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and for the use of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) in Belgrade on 15 March. The protesters also observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign.

On 30 March 2025, citizens marched through Valjevo, demanding accountability for the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The protesters voiced the newest students' demands regarding the investigation of police actions in Belgrade on 15 March and called for the citizens' support.

On 29 March 2025, residents of Sysert, Sverdlovsk and a nearby village protested and filmed a video addressed to the acting regional governor. Locals spoke out against the construction of a waste sorting landfill in the area. People of Sysert and nearby settlements have been sporadically taking to the streets with similar concerns since the fall of 2023.

On 29 March 2025, more than 100 animal rights activists protested on the Leonova street in Kaliningrad. Protesters spoke out against the controversial parliamentary 'stray animals euthanasia' bill that is being discussed in the State Duma. Recently it was uncovered that not only stray animals, but also lost pets could be killed within the framework of the proposed legislation.

On 29 March 2025, residents of the town and the Bogorodskiy district protested and filmed a video addressed to the local authorities in Balashikha, Moscow Oblast. Locals complained about the pollution of the local river by the nearby factories and demanded that the local authorities address the problem.

On 29 March 2025, more than 50 animal rights activists protested in Rostov-on-Don. Protesters spoke out against the controversial parliamentary 'stray animals euthanasia' bill that is being discussed in the State Duma. Recently it was uncovered that not only stray animals, but also lost pets could be killed within the framework of the proposed legislation.

On 29 March 2025, students and citizens gathered in front of the 'Informer', a pro-regime media outlet in Belgrade - Vozdovac, protesting against constant disinformation and targeting of students and the academic community. The protesters demanded that the media be removed from Belgrade frequencies and called out the editor-in-chief.
On 29 March 2025, citizens gathered in Futog to initiate the local plenum and denounce the SNS meeting occurring at the local community premises.

On 29 March 2025, students gathered in Novi Sad, voicing their dissatisfaction and concerns with the physical attacks on their colleagues. The protest is triggered by the recent beating of Faculty of Sports students after a night out, most probably by SNS affiliates. The protesters also observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, commemorating and seeking accountability for the Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse.

Around 26 March 2025 (as reported), an investigation was published that highlighted a military base that is suspectedly used to store Russian nuclear weapons near Asipovichy (Osipovichskiy, Mogilev). On a photo that was taken at the military unit and published by the Belarusian military, a dosimeter interface can be seen. The town of Asipovichy and a nearby areas are not on the list of territories of the region contaminated with radionuclides as a result of the Chernobyl disaster, and there are no nuclear power facilities nearby, therefore an appearance of a dosimeter at the military base is highly unusual. The military unit is utilized by the Belarusian artillery and missile regiments, and the base itself is used to store various munitions. In 2024 several reports suspected that the base that at that moment was being extended near Asipovichy could serve as a potential nuclear weapons storing facility.

On 24 March 2025, citizens and students marched, blocked roads, and gathered at several locations in Belgrade, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The protesters also commemorated the anniversary of the NATO bombing of the Socialist Republic (SR) of Yugoslavia, and paid tribute to the civilian victims.

On 24 March 2025, students and citizens gathered in front of the police station in Cacak, condemning the police's lack of response and adequate reaction to the physical attack on students in the blockade, who were injured on 22 March. Protesters demanded accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. Protesters also observed 16 minutes of noise, protesting the police authorities' use of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) in Belgrade on 15 March. On the same day, teachers, students, and parents gathered in front of the Ministry of Education also to demand accountability for the canopy collapse.

On 24 March 2025, high school and faculty students, parents, and citizens gathered in front of two high schools in Kragujevac, protesting the directors' decision to resume the school year and ignore the students' demands.

On 24 March 2025, teachers gathered in front of the rectorate in Kragujevac, displaying their support for their colleagues enduring political pressures, threats, and attacks for supporting the students' demands and faculty blockades.

On 24 March 2025, students and citizens marched through Novi Sad, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The protesters observed an additional minute, commemorating the anniversary of the NATO bombing of the Socialist Republic (SR) of Yugoslavia, and paid tribute to the civilian victims.

On 24 March 2025, citizens and opposition representatives gathered in front of the Municipality building in Belgrade - Zvezdara, protesting against the police and private security forces who prevented the opposition members and citizens from entering the municipal session.
On 24 March 2025, citizens protested in Kraljevo, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 24 March 2025, parents gathered in front of the 'Sonja Marinkovic' school in Novi Sad, supporting students and professors in a blockade and demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse. A group of parents, among whom SNS representatives were present, counter-protested and demanded that the school year resume.

On 24 March 2025, students, teachers, parents, and citizens gathered in front of the 'Laza Kostic' school in Novi Sad, voicing their support for the students' blockade, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 24 March 2025, teachers, students, and parents gathered in front of the Ministry of Education in Belgrade - Savski Venac, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. On 23 March 2025, an individual affiliated with SNS attacked a BIRN journalist during a reportage in Belgrade - Zvezdara, who endeavoured to get footage of the verbal skirmish between the SNS political activists and protesters supporting students.

On 23 March 2025, in the early morning, an unidentified perpetrator fired gunshots at the apartment of a local citizens' association leader and local government MP, who supports student protests. The individual believes that the motive behind the attack is his activism and support for students in Nis.

On 23 March 2025, farmers with their tractors, citizens, and students, engaged in a protest ride, march, and road blockages in Obrenovac, protesting against corruption and demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse. The protesters also voiced that corruption is the main culprit behind tragic events in Serbia, North Macedonia, and Greece.

On 23 March 2025, citizens and students marched through the city and gathered in front of the Assembly building in Cacak, protesting against the ruling MPs who prevented their participation in the earlier Assembly sessions. Several citizens entered the building, but the police forces promptly formed a buffer and prevented the rest of the protesters from entering. The protesters also condemned the police's lack of response to the attack on students in the blockade the earlier night.

On 23 March 2025, citizens and students blocked the local transportation company depot in Smederevo, protesting against their decision to call off the transportation of students to Belgrade on 15 March.
On 23 March 2025, citizens gathered in Backa Palanka, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 23 March 2025, citizens gathered in Belgrade - Vracar, protesting against SNS activists' presence in their municipality, who set up their party booth to promote SNS political activities. Protesters sang and shouted against SNS, leading to them departing their booth with police escort.

On 23 March 2025, citizens gathered in Belgrade - Zvezdara, protesting against SNS activists' presence in their municipality, who set up their party booth to promote SNS political activities. Police forces were present and protected SNS representatives.

On 23 March 2025, citizens gathered to organize the local plenum in Stara Pazova and to voice their support for the students' demands for accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 23 March 2025, citizens gathered at multiple Local Governmental Units (LGUs) to organize the local plenum in Zrenjanin and to voice their support for the students' demands, seeking accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 23 March 2025, students, teachers, health workers, farmers, bikers, and citizens gathered and blocked roads in Subotica, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse, and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The protesters voiced their issues with staged criminal complaints targeting students and unpaid salaries for teachers.

On 23 March 2025, teachers and students marched through Nis, protesting against the police custody of their fellow student protesters during the earlier protests. The protesters also observed 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 22 March 2025, several hundred citizens and teachers marched through Leskovac, protesting against the dismissal of their fellow citizen for supporting the student protests in Belgrade. The individual worked for Serbia's Pension and Disability Insurance institution in Leskovac, and after multiple threats to his family and workplace blackmail, he got officially fired following the Belgrade protests on 15 March. The protesters initially marched through the city but subsequently gathered in front of the National Theater where the President held a meeting with citizens who supported him. Police forces formed a buffer to separate the protesters from the President and his supporters.

On 22 March 2025, students and citizens blocked roads in Belgrade - Savski Venac, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The protesters voiced that they do not accept becoming 'targets', alluding to the frequent attacks directed towards them and the incident on March 15, when the police forces activated Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) against the crowd. Protesters observed an additional minute to pay their respects to the victims of the Kocani fire in North Macedonia.

On 22 March 2025, students and citizens marched through Prokuplje, calling for accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. One citizen held a speech, which the students later condemned and distanced themselves from the individual due to hateful content.

On 22 March 2025, citizens and students gathered in Ruma, observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse.

On 22 March 2025, citizens and activists gathered in front of the Ministry of Agriculture in Belgrade - Novi Beograd, voicing their concerns about the state of animals in Serbia, and the lack of appropriate legislation that would ensure animal welfare.

On 22 March 2025, a group of unidentified rioters attacked a group of students in the blockade in Cacak, injuring at least four students, who subsequently sought medical attention. The event marks one of the many pressures and physical attacks on students across Serbia.
On 22 March 2025, citizens gathered in Belgrade - Zvezdara, protesting against SNS activists' presence in their municipality, who set up their party booth to promote SNS political activities.

On 22 March 2025, citizens gathered in Lazarevac, protesting against SNS threats and blackmails to citizens supporting the students and demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse. Citizens also gathered within the local plenum, which is one of the students' recommendations to exercise direct democracy.

On 21 March 2025, either Russian or Ukrainian forces blew up or shelled with artillery the building of the 'Sudzha' gas measuring station that is located next to the border checkpoint near Oleshnya (Sudzhanskiy, Kursk). Casualties unknown. The station was severely damaged. Both sides accused each other: Russia accused Ukraine of blowing the station up and breaking the verbal agreement between the two sides to cease fire on objects of energy infrastructure, Ukraine accused Russian of shelling the station with the goal of blaming Ukraine for breaking the agreement. The station is part of the gas pipeline that until January 2025 was used to transfer gas internationally to Europe through Ukraine.
On 21 March 2025, Ukrainian military shelled with artillery the town of Sudzha (Sudzhanskiy, Kursk). No casualties, Russian reporters, who were at the site, managed to evade the strikes.

On 21 March 2025, citizens and students marched and blocked roads in Belgrade, demanding accountability for the victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse, and observing 16 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The protest was triggered by the information about the 16th victim of the incident, a 19-year-old student who was in a coma for four months.

On 21 March 2025, in the early morning, students commenced their blockade of the public transportation depot in Belgrade - Novi Beograd, demanding accountability for the 15 victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse and supporting the general workers' strike.

On 21 March 2025, residents gathered in front of the Municipality in Belgrade - Stari Grad, making loud noises as a protest against the local authorities' use of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) in Belgrade on 15 March. Citizens initiated implementing one of the students' recommendations, which is exercising direct democracy through forming local plenums.

On 21 March 2025, computer sciences students marched through Belgrade and gathered in front of their faculty in Belgrade - Stari Grad, protesting against the local authorities' pressures towards the students in blockades and the faculty's initiated disciplinary procedures against them.

On 21 March 2025, an unidentified individual punched a woman municipal employee in Belgrade - Vozdovac, who sustained head trauma. The reason behind the attack was that the individual wanted to attend the assembly session, which the employee refused.

On 21 March 2025, a large number of students and citizens gathered in front of the City House in Nis, protesting against the meeting between the local authorities and SNS high officials in this city. The protesters made loud noises in dissent of the local authorities' use of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) in Belgrade on 15 March, and threw eggs, flour, and water at the officials, including the Mayor of Nis and director of the Health Center. Consequently, SNS canceled the meeting because of the protest.

Police forces protected the entrance and dispersed the protesters, additionally arresting another individual.

On 21 March 2025, students, teachers, and citizens marched through Novi Sad, seeking answers and official confirmation on the sound device used against the protesters in Belgrade on 15 March. The students also raised concerns about the numerous health implications following the device activation - which was confirmed to be a Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) by many domestic and international analysts.

Property destruction: On 19 March 2025, an unidentified perpetrator punctured the tires of University professors' cars in Belgrade - Novi Beograd. The incident is deliberate, given that other cars were parked at the same place, and only the professors' cars were damaged. Professors believe that the ruling regime is trying to scare them because of their support for the students' demands.

On 19 March 2025, teachers gathered in front of the Radio Television of Serbia (RTS) building in Belgrade - Palilula, demanding objective and truthful information, and support for the democratization of the Serbian society. The teachers voiced that they want to be heard alongside students and the rest of the Serbian public seeking societal development.

On 19 March 2025, students, teachers, citizens, and activists gathered in front of the City Administration in Bor, demanding justice for Lazar Dinic, a member of 'STAV' civil society organization, arrested under a presumption of 'organizing violence in the Assembly building' during the Belgrade protests on 15 March. Dinic is also accused of being a member of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA).

On 19 March 2025, citizens and students gathered in front of the police station in Cacak, making loud noises in protest against the authorities' utilization of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) against the citizens in Belgrade on 15 March.

On 19 March 2025, teachers, students, parents, and citizens gathered in front of the 'Stanislav Sremcevic' school in Kragujevac, voicing their support for the teacher injured after being exposed to a Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) in Belgrade on 15 March.

On 19 March 2025, citizens and teachers marched through Kraljevo, supporting the students' demands for accountability for the 15 victims of the Novi Sad railway station's canopy collapse. The protesters also made noise in their condemnation of state-authorities use of Long Range Acoustic Device (LRAD) on peacefully protesting citizens.

On 19 March 2025, a large number of citizens and SPP representatives gathered in front of the City Assembly in Mladenovac, condemning the MP's support for the individuals acting as 'Students that want to study' who counter-protested against the actual students' demands in Belgrade. The protesters spilled flour in front of the building, and marked the direction for prosecutors and judges, 'showing the way where they have to intervene'.

On 19 March 2025, high-school art students gathered in front of their school in Nis, protesting against the director's lack of support for their demands and the fact that she broke through the student blockade with the police.

On 19 March 2025, health workers protested in Novi Sad, under the slogan 'patients are not political props', condemning President Vucic's visit of intensive care patients who were transferred to Belgrade following the Kocani fire. The protesters deem the visits and photographs as 'cheap political points'.

On 19 March 2025, citizens gathered in front of the Municipality building in Sid, protesting against the local officials and condemning their lack of support for students' demands and their loyalty to the regime. The citizens also voiced that they wanted to participate in the assembly sessions but without success.

On 19 March 2025, health workers protested in Sremska Kamenica, under the slogan 'patients are not political props', condemning President Vucic's visit of intensive care patients who were transferred to Belgrade following the Kocani fire. The protesters deem the visits and photographs as 'cheap political points'.

On 19 March 2025, citizens gathered in front of the City Administration in Sremska Mitrovica, protesting against the state officials who supported the individuals acting under the parole 'Students that want to study' (former Students 2.0) closely affiliated with SNS. The protesters labeled such actions as 'shameful' and 'anti-Serbian youth', threw eggs at the officials, and even spat at the incumbent Mayor.

notes: On 18 March 2025, from the morning to the evening, in attempts to cross the international border, Ukrainian forces, supported by drones, attacked Russian positions 5 times at 2 locations across the Krasnoyaruzhskiy district, including into the direction of Demidovka, Belgorod. According to the Russian war reporters, in the evening, Ukrainian troops managed to marginally advance towards Demidovka, but failed to approach the settlement. Ukrainian aviation struck the 3rd Motorized Rifle Division of the 20th Army command post around Demidovka (Krasnoyaruzhskiy, Belgorod). Russian MoD reported in the evening that up to 200 soldiers, 24 armored vehicles and 5 engineering vehicles took part in the assault, all the attacks were repelled by the Russian troops, who were supported by artillery and aviation, and that 60 Ukrainian soldiers died, 8 armored vehicles, 1 car, and 3 engineering vehicles were destroyed, near Demidovka and Prilesye. According to the Russian mil influencers, by midday around 20 Ukrainian soldiers died. [Russian MoD reported 60 fatalities. Coded as 10 fatalities split across 2 events. 5 fatalities coded to this event]. Some Russian sources timed the attack to the Trump-Putin telephone talks that were happening on the same day.

On 18 March 2025, students and citizens gathered and blocked the main square in Nis, observing 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign in support of students demanding accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the train station in Novi Sad. The protesters added another 60 minutes of silence commemorating the victims of the Kocani fire and also supported the Novi Sad students who were confronted by the police in their attempt to block the Assembly the earlier night.

On 18 March 2025, students, citizens, and opposition representatives gathered in front of the City Assembly in Novi Sad, protesting against the 'illegally convened sessions with 160 agenda items'. After police intervened the earlier night and dispersed the students from the entrance, citizens and opposition members joined the students in front of the Assembly and condemned the police intervention towards students.
